purpose: Restore documentation-backed Integration Fabric promotions and inline vendor value reviews lost during FORGE convergence. Entries are copied from previously reviewed evidence overlays; no maturity inflation, tenant certification or write authority is introduced.

patch.evidenceNote: IFS Cloud officially exposes REST APIs using OData, with OpenAPI v2/v3 specifications available from API Explorer. Premium and Integration APIs are preferred for system integrations; Entity Service APIs can expose entity models for CRUD/state transitions but require administrator activation. Projection permission sets support read-only access, which is the required WFM starting posture. No tenant authentication was attempted.

requiredPermissions: OAuth 2.0 identity scoped to required API projections
read-only projection permission sets wherever available
no Entity Service mutation permissions during discovery
dataAvailableOrExpected: tenant-exposed OData entity sets and projection data
ERP/manufacturing entity data exposed by authorised Premium, Integration or Entity Service APIs
automationOpportunities: production-demand refresh from authorised ERP projections
cost-centre and organisation synchronisation
approved labour/cost export only after write-roundtrip certification
customerValue: faster ERP integration through published OData/OpenAPI contracts
savingsHypotheses: reduce manual finance and production-data reconciliation
reduce implementation effort by reusing stable published projections
reduce overstaffing when production demand can be read from IFS
dataGaps: exact enabled projections and manufacturing objects are tenant/version specific
custom projections require customer-specific mapping
constraintsRisks: Entity Service APIs require administrator activation
deprecated API versions must not be selected for new adapters
write-capable entity services remain disabled in WFM

patch.evidenceNote: Epicor documents Kinetic Open REST API as platform-level access to ERP services, data and business logic. The API is OData v4-compliant, versioned, discoverable through built-in REST help, and protected by API keys, access scopes and ERP user/data permissions. This provides a usable route for manufacturing orders, resources, costs and related ERP context once a customer tenant is authorised. No tenant authentication was attempted.

requiredPermissions: API key restricted by access scope
ERP user/data permissions limited to required read services
no business-logic execution permission during discovery unless separately required
dataAvailableOrExpected: manufacturing/order/resource/cost context exposed by the customer's enabled ERP services
automationOpportunities: production/order changes can trigger labour-plan recalculation once representative reads are proven
approved labour/cost feedback can be considered only after controlled write certification
customerValue: faster implementation through OData-compatible service discovery
savingsHypotheses: identify labour variance against manufacturing demand
reduce duplicate production-data entry
reduce planning latency between ERP order changes and workforce schedules
dataGaps: available business objects and customisations vary by Kinetic tenant/version
resource and labour semantics require canonical mapping validation
constraintsRisks: API key access must also be constrained by Epicor access scopes and ERP permissions
service versions and customer customisations require compatibility testing

patch.evidenceNote: Ignition 8.3 documents a dynamically generated OpenAPI/REST interface at /openapi and /openapi.json, OPC UA client/server connectivity, and Edge IIoT MQTT publication. HTTP API tokens can reach mutative routes and vendor guidance warns they can modify configuration, tags or projects, so WFM must use a segregated read-only facade or equivalent gateway controls rather than assuming a token alone is least privilege. No plant or tenant connection was attempted.

requiredPermissions: read-only tag/telemetry access through a segregated facade or equivalent policy boundary
OPC UA/MQTT subscription rights limited to required namespaces/topics
no Gateway configuration/project/tag mutation rights
dataAvailableOrExpected: industrial tags and machine/process state made available through OPC UA
Gateway API metadata exposed through documented OpenAPI routes
automationOpportunities: machine-stop events can trigger labour redeployment recommendations
machine restart/recovery can trigger staffing recall recommendations
correlate staffed time with machine state and output evidence
savingsHypotheses: reduce paid idle time during equipment stops
reduce labour waiting for unavailable machines
quantify labour cost of downtime by shift/work centre
dataGaps: tag names and semantics are site-specific
machine output/OEE meaning requires customer asset mapping
timestamps and historian retention require site validation
constraintsRisks: Ignition API tokens may reach mutative HTTP API routes
plant-network connectivity must terminate at a controlled site-edge boundary
WFM must not issue PLC/tag writes or control methods by default

patch.evidenceNote: HighByte documents a REST Data Server that can browse and request contextualized industrial data, plus native MQTT v3.1.1/v5 with Sparkplug support, OPC UA, Modbus, SQL, files/SFTP and Kafka/cloud connections. Its REST surface can be read/write, so WFM must use role-based read-only access and keep OT writes disabled. No tenant or edge authentication was attempted.

requiredPermissions: role-scoped REST Data Server read access
MQTT/Sparkplug subscription rights limited to required namespaces
OPC UA browse/read/subscribe only
no underlying OT write or callable-pipeline mutation rights
dataAvailableOrExpected: time-series, transactional and master data exposed through configured HighByte connections
automationOpportunities: machine-stop and recovery signals can trigger labour redeployment/recovery recommendations
use one governed OT API/UNS route instead of bespoke direct machine integrations
correlate staffed time, output and equipment state by work centre
savingsHypotheses: reduce paid idle labour during equipment disruption
reduce site-integration engineering effort by reusing an existing industrial data layer
reduce duplicated point-to-point OT integrations
dataGaps: customer namespaces, models and tag semantics are site-specific
available data depends on connections already configured in the customer's HighByte deployment
constraintsRisks: REST Data Server can write to underlying connections, so read-only policy must be technically enforced
Sparkplug birth/death and session semantics must be preserved
plant connectivity must stay behind the customer-controlled edge boundary
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Build a HighByte thin adapter on the existing REST/MQTT/OPC UA profiles, validate Sparkplug birth/death handling with fixtures, then seek a customer sandbox or lab tenant for authenticated read round-trip proof.

patch.evidenceNote: SAP's 2026 Fieldglass REST API General Reference Guide documents authenticated GET/POST/PUT integration resources over HTTPS with OAuth 2.0, client credentials, certificate and SAML-based authentication options. It explicitly references Connector, Identity (SCIM) and Reporting APIs, with an optional x-ApplicationKey depending on tenant/API. SAP's connector library also documents active-worker downloads and customer-specific contingent-workforce configurations such as custom fields, qualifications, rates and accounting mappings. No SAP Fieldglass sandbox or tenant authentication was attempted.

requiredPermissions: OAuth 2.0 client scoped to required Fieldglass REST/connector/reporting reads
optional tenant/application key only where the selected API requires it
worker/download permissions limited to required contingent-workforce data
PII, rates and accounting data minimised to the implemented WFM workflow
no upload, approval or worker mutation permission during discovery
dataAvailableOrExpected: active and contingent worker records exposed by authorised downloads/APIs
custom fields and qualifications where configured
rates and cost/accounting references where authorised
identity records through Fieldglass identity/SCIM integration where enabled
automationOpportunities: contingent-worker joiner/mover/leaver synchronisation
agency-labour availability and cost visibility
qualification-aware external-worker scheduling
approved worker/time/cost lifecycle write-back only after separate sandbox and write-roundtrip certification
integration exception monitoring through audit/reporting data
customerValue: better agency and worker cost attribution
improved visibility of contingent workforce alongside employed labour
savingsHypotheses: reduce manual contingent-worker setup and reconciliation
reduce avoidable agency spend by exposing worker/rate/qualification context to planning
reduce compliance risk from incomplete qualification or worker-status data
reduce payroll/invoice exceptions caused by inconsistent external-worker master data
dataGaps: enabled connector/API resources and fields vary by buyer configuration
custom fields, qualifications, security IDs, rates and accounting mappings are customer-specific
some Fieldglass integrations remain file/connector based rather than a single normalized REST object model
constraintsRisks: REST resources support POST/PUT as well as GET, so read-only access must be enforced by permission and connector design
worker/rate/accounting data is sensitive and requires narrow retention and logging
OAuth tokens can have varying API access and must not be treated as least privilege by default
tenant region/environment URLs and test-environment availability vary
duplicate worker records can arise from customer segmentation/configuration and require deterministic identity reconciliation
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Build a Fieldglass thin adapter over the existing REST/SCIM/file profiles, starting with OAuth token acquisition and read-only connector/reporting discovery; add canonical external-worker, qualification and rate mappings plus duplicate/segmentation handling, then seek an authorised SAP Fieldglass test tenant for authenticated read-roundtrip proof.

patch.evidenceNote: Tulip documents scoped REST APIs for Tables, Users/Operators, Stations and Machine Attributes, plus HTTP/SQL/MQTT connectors and OPC UA-backed machine data. API service accounts use key/secret credentials via HTTP Basic Auth with granular scopes such as tables:read; write endpoints and documented endpoint rate limits remain separately gated. No tenant authentication was attempted.

read scopes for tables/users/stations required by the workflow
machine/production read access only
no users:write or machine write scope during discovery

savingsHypotheses: reduce duplicate shop-floor data entry

patch.evidenceNote: Celigo's 2026 platform documentation adds a hosted MCP management surface over Streamable HTTP using bearer API tokens, operating on the same integration resources as the REST API. Celigo also documents network policies and scoped token/access controls. This is useful for autonomous implementation orchestration, but it is a management plane and must not be treated as permission for unsupervised production mutations. No Celigo tenant authentication was attempted.

requiredPermissions: custom-scoped API token rather than full access
network policy restricting allowed callers
read-only/account-observation capabilities during discovery
separate approval for flow, connection or resource mutations
dataAvailableOrExpected: logs and execution state exposed by integrator.io APIs
MCP tool/resource metadata for configured Celigo capabilities
automationOpportunities: autonomous implementation can inspect existing Celigo integration resources
reuse customer flows/connectors rather than create duplicate point-to-point integrations
surface integration failures into WFM support automation
customerValue: faster zero-human implementation where Celigo is already present
reuse of existing customer iPaaS investment
savingsHypotheses: reduce implementation engineering time
reduce duplicate connector build/maintenance
shorten diagnosis of integration failures
dataGaps: available MCP tools depend on account configuration and entitlements
business data semantics still depend on connected upstream systems
constraintsRisks: MCP/REST management capabilities can mutate production integration resources
unrestricted tokens or servers may expose more capability than WFM needs
regional Celigo environments must be bound explicitly
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Model Celigo MCP as a separately governed management-plane adapter, first with tool/resource discovery only; add a reusable MCP transport profile only after read-only capability enforcement and sandbox behaviour are verified.
